steps.title: Acknowledges God as "a revealer of secrets"
steps.detail: The confession costs him nothing and does not outlast the chapter. The same court that hears it will be ordered to worship an image in Daniel 3, and the king who said it will be the one giving the order.

steps.title: Acknowledges God as "able to deliver"
steps.detail: The words in verse 17 belong to the three Hebrews, not to the king. His own verdict comes at 3:29, and it still leaves the image he set up standing in the plain of Dura.

steps.title: Acknowledges God as "the King of heaven"
steps.detail: Only the third confession is spoken by a man with nothing left to defend, and only this one ends in praise rather than policy. The chapter closes with the king restored and the throne still God's to give.

steps.title: The Tall Cosmic Tree
points: Reached to heaven
Sheltered all beasts and birds
Symbol of imperial majesty
Nebuchadnezzar in his glory

steps.title: The Banded Stump
points: Stripped of branches and fruit
Driven into the dew and grass
Bound with iron and bronze
The king humbled, yet preserved by grace

steps.title: "I have built"
steps.detail: The boast is the mirror of Daniel 2:37, where the same prophet told him that God had given him a kingdom, power, and strength, and glory. Every clause here takes one of those back.

steps.title: "By the might of my power"
steps.detail: The kingdom that verse 17 says the Most High gives to whomsoever he will is claimed here as the work of one man's arm.

steps.title: "For the honour of my majesty"
steps.text: Steals the glory due to God alone.
steps.detail: The sentence is still in his mouth when the voice falls from heaven, and the seven times begin. The rest of the chapter is written by a king who has learned the first two clauses were borrowed.

steps.title: Nebuchadnezzar lifts his eyes to heaven

s4-6.title: The Emperor of Babylon / The King of Glory

steps.title: Nebuchadnezzar
points: A man who set up an image and commanded worship
"Is not this great Babylon, that I have built for the house of the kingdom by the might of my power, and for the honour of my majesty?"
Exalted himself on his palace roof
Driven into the dust as a beast
Humbled by force under divine wrath
Restored only after crushing judgment

steps.title: Jesus Christ
points: God incarnate who took the form of man
"Not my will, but Thine be done"
Humbled Himself to the death of the cross
Laid in a manger; buried in a borrowed tomb
Emptied Himself willingly in sacrificial love
Highly exalted by the Father above every name
